claims.explanation: Desoxycortone is a mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2) agonist, and its selective antiproliferative effect likely depends on NR3C2 expression, since lines lacking the receptor cannot transduce the steroid signal. The transcriptional response (STAT3, NFATC3, CHEK1 up; CDC20, CCNB2 down) suggests mineralocorticoid-receptor activation perturbs cell-cycle and STAT3/NFAT-dependent survival programs, so selectivity is expected in lines with intact NR3C2 signaling and without protective NR3C1/glucocorticoid-receptor buffering.

features.basis: drug is an NR3C2 agonist; receptor expression is required for response
glucocorticoid receptor signaling can oppose mineralocorticoid effects and buffer steroid response
STAT3 is induced in the virtual cell response and supports steroid-dependent survival signaling
CCNB2 is repressed by the drug; high baseline expression may sustain proliferation and reduce killing
CDC20 is repressed by the drug; high baseline expression supports mitotic progression and resistance
CHEK1 upregulation indicates DNA-damage/checkpoint engagement contributing to growth inhibition
NFATC3 is induced in the virtual cell response and may mediate steroid-dependent transcriptional killing
KIT is induced in the virtual cell response, marking a responsive lineage context
SOX2 induction in the virtual cell response may reflect a stem-like survival program
serotonin-receptor pathway is the most transcriptionally similar drug class and steroid pathways intersect serotonin signaling
serotonin-receptor pathway similarity suggests HTR2B context may modulate response
desoxycortone was identified as a potential TNFRSF25-pathway modulator in docking, linking it to apoptosis signaling
